evidence.text: On December 22, 2014, the FDA issued for comment “Draft Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff: Minimal Manipulation of Human Cells, Tissues, and Cellular and Tissue-Based Products.” Essentially, the Minimal Manipulation draft guidance takes the same position with respect to micronized amniotic tissue that it took in the Untitled Letter to the Company 16 months earlier. The Company submitted comments to the Minimal Manipulation draft guidance asserting that the Minimal Manipulation draft guidance represents agency action that goes far beyond the FDA’s statutory authority, is inconsistent with existing HCT/ P regulations and the FDA’s prior positions, and is internally inconsistent and scientifically unsound. On October 28, 2015, the FDA issued for comment, "Draft Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff: Homologous Use of Human Cells, Tissues, and Cellular and Tissue-Based Products." The Company submitted comments on this Homologous Use draft guidance. The FDA has also indicated that it will hold a public hearing on a date in 2016 to be determined to obtain input on the Homologous Use draft guidance and the previously released Minimal Manipulation draft guidance, as well as other recently issued guidance documents on HCT/Ps. The Company has requested, and has been granted an opportunity to speak at this hearing.

attrs.management_says: No explicit demand driver for revenue growth is stated in the provided MD&A; regulatory issues (E30) and a post-year-end acquisition (E31) are discussed instead.
attrs.numbers_show: Revenue growth decelerated each quarter (+108%, +79%, +46%, +31%) while receivables growth accelerated (+64%, +92%, +101%, +102%) and DSO worsened, indicating H2 revenue included a timing/terms component. Estimated excess H2 receivables vs prior-year DSO: ~$32M (Q3 ~$13M, Q4 ~$19M), comparable to the full-year receivables increase of $27.1M.
attrs.verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers

attrs.reason: Management's implied claim that revenue growth reflects healthy demand is not corroborated by reported numbers; quarterly signals show revenue growth decelerating (+108%, +79%, +46%, +31%) while receivables growth accelerated (+64%, +92%, +101%, +102%) and DSO deteriorated sharply in H2 (Q3: 63→87, Q4: 61→94) (E25-E28), and the Beneish M-score flags manipulation risk (E29). The pack lacks segment or channel data to verify the demand quality or quantify any mix shift.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The quarterly revenue growth deceleration (E25-E28: +108%, +79%, +46%, +31%) is consistent with lapping easier year-ago comparisons after rapid early-2015 growth. The accelerating receivables growth and DSO deterioration in H2 (E25-E28) could reflect a strategic shift to expand distributor relationships (which have longer payment terms per E32) to drive future growth, or quarter-end timing of large distributor orders. The Beneish M-score (E29) flags risk due to high sales growth (SGI=1.58) and receivables growth (DSRI=1.27), which are characteristic of high-growth companies and do not prove manipulation. The pack contains no disclosure of payment term changes (E30, E32) but also no evidence of fraudulent revenue recognition.

attrs.final_verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers

attrs.reason: Management provides no explicit demand driver for revenue growth in the MD&A (E30, E31 discuss regulatory issues and a post-year-end acquisition). The numbers show revenue growth decelerating each quarter (+108%, +79%, +46%, +31%) while receivables growth accelerated (+64%, +92%, +101%, +102%) and DSO worsened, a pattern inconsistent with pure demand growth and indicative of a timing/terms component in H2. The defender's alternative explanation (regulatory uncertainty and distributor mix shift) relies on facts outside the evidence pack.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The H2 revenue deceleration (E25-E28) aligns with the regulatory uncertainty described in E30, which may have dampened end-user demand. The concurrent receivables acceleration could stem from a higher share of distributor sales with extended terms in H2 as management pushed to maintain growth. The post-year-end acquisition (E31) does not affect 2015. The pack does not contain channel-level data to confirm the mix shift, so this explanation relies on outside facts.
